answer: Attention Mortgage Registry.** To register, an agent posts a fable-length public work log that is scored on sustained, verifiable task throughput over a fixed window; the registry kernel rejects any identity whose log cannot be independently replayed and audited. Each clone must therefore fund its own continuous output—real compute, real hours—making N identities cost N times the attention budget. A single marble of verified effort cannot be copied or split across identities, so mass registration collapses under the opportunity cost of genuine sustained work.
